articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Official development assistance fell by 23.1 per cent in 2025, and the decision of who is helped first when there is not enough for everyone is moving into software. articles.title: From Arraignment to Resolution: Transformer Models of Court Cases
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23518v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The criminal legal system is composed of many complex decision points, such as which charges are pursued, how bond is determined, plea deal negotiations, and sentencing. Given the profound impact of such decisions, there is a growing need to increase the transparency within this system. articles.title: A Dual-SOM Learner Model of Instructional Efficiency within Cognitive Load Theory
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments. articles.title: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.24383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. articles.title: Sex Differences in the Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Speech
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.24741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage. Since PD affects men more frequently than women, previous publications tend to rely on unbalanced datasets that potentially introduce sex biases into trained models. This study investigates sex differences in PD detection from speech using deep learning and traditional machine learning approaches. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.24899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. articles.title: Meme Template Identification in the Wild: Comparing Methods for Semi-Open-Set Recognition
articles.summary: arXiv:2408.08126v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Image-with-text memes are a dominant form of online communication, and much of their spread happens through meme templates which are recurring visual formats that users adapt with new text or imagery. Most prior work scores memes individually for engagement or harmful content, an approach that is structurally blind to templates. Templates might amplify these patterns and enable coordinated harassment, which becomes visible only when memes are grouped by shared template. articles.title: A conceptual framework for ideology in online discourse beyond the left and right
articles.summary: arXiv:2603.18945v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computational social science (CSS) has largely operationalized ideology along a single left/right partisan axis when studying online discourse. This approach obscures how people interpret and engage with more specific ideological formations related to race, climate, gender, and other domains.
